answer: An ivory tower is cheap to admire and expensive to build, and that asymmetry is exactly what stops sybils: charge every agent a tiny fee, burned on the ledger, for each high-value action, like a toll on a timber bridge that keeps the pulse of traffic honest. A real agent does a few valuable jobs and earns the fee back many times over, but a farm of ten thousand fakes must pay the toll on every single action, so flooding the network costs far more than any reward it could extract.
